content:
The image shows a corn leaf/stalk with:
- A dark reddish-brown to purple/black elongated lesion along what appears to be the midrib or stalk area
- Small black oval/round spots arranged in a line within the reddish-brown zone
- Yellow spotting visible on the surrounding green leaf tissue
- The black spots are embedded in the dark reddish tissue and appear to follow a linear pattern along the midrib

This matches **Physoderma Brown Spot** closely: the description mentions "dark purplish to black oval spots on the midrib" with yellow spots on the leaf blade. The dark spots arranged linearly along the midrib within a reddish-brown zone, combined with yellowish spots scattered on the surrounding leaf tissue, is the classic presentation.

The black spots arranged in a line along the midrib are characteristic of Physoderma, distinguishing it from rust (which would have scattered pustules on leaf surfaces, not concentrated on the midrib in this linear pattern).
